extracted.intended_audience: general reading public interested in manners, education, conversation, dancing, friendship, and literary taste (parents, young people, aspiring writers/readers)
extracted.subtask_short: advice on manners and literary taste
extracted.subtask_description: A set of prescriptive and evaluative principles about educating children (esp. girls), good-breeding and dancing, qualities of friendship and conversation, and standards for heroic poetry and popular writing. The page mixes practical conduct guidance with literary-criticism criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of bodily and mental education
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not attend only to the person or only to the mind; in daughters parents often care for persons and neglect minds, while in sons they adorn minds and neglect bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general mistake in educating children leads to women celebrated for person but neglected in mental cultivation and boys who are shy or ill-prepared in social situations. Parents should aim to cultivate both aspects rather than privileging appearance or intellect alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make mind and body improve together
rubrics_metrics.description: The true art is to make the Mind and Body improve together; make Gesture follow Thought, not Thought employed upon Gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: Cleomira's elegant motion accompanies simplicity and innocence of thought, producing admiration without provoking improper expectations. Education should align bodily carriage with inward virtue so that outward grace expresses inward qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate dancing for graceful comportment
rubrics_metrics.description: A moderate knowledge of dancing and the little rules of good-breeding is extremely useful, as it gives a graceful carriage and assurance in company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting Cowley and a school proposal: teach just enough dancing 'for foul weather' or to gain a graceful comportment—beyond that is superfluous or worse. Dancing helps one enter a room with good grace and avoid unseemly approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation learned from dancing-masters
rubrics_metrics.description: If you add nothing of your own to what dancing-masters teach (and what they often do not know), you risk becoming an affected fop rather than a well-bred person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dancing-masters regulate external matters, but one must internalize and personalize conduct; mere mechanical imitation of taught steps without inward judgement produces affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware corruptions and indecent dances
rubrics_metrics.description: Some dances and steps have grown into corrupt or lascivious practices (e.g., 'setting', certain 'kissing dances', or theatrical capers), which are improper especially for young women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a father's shock at 'setting' and a 'Mol Patley' turn that exposed too much; father extracting daughter mid-dance. Country dancing contains familiarities that can lead to dangerous consequences, so parents and guardians should be vigilant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-dance moral/educational uses and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Country dancing includes emblematical figures composed for the instruction of youth (e.g., 'Hunt the Squirrel' recommends modesty and discretion), and can be practised innocently when observed with proper restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a domestic invention in the country, it is widely practised and may be harmless if kept moderate; but familiarity between sexes during such dances may sometimes prove dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: First impressions and outward comportment matter
rubrics_metrics.description: We generally form lasting ideas of people at first sight; one should avoid anything disagreeable or uncomely in approaching others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decent, graceful approach and knowledge of small rules of good-breeding gives assurance and eases social interaction; lack of such knowledge can embarrass even learned men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation scale: intimacy yields depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Large companies produce general and formal talk; the freest, most instructive, and unreserved discourse occurs between two intimate friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In small clubs conversation becomes more particular and free; two friends disclose private opinions, test sentiments' strength, and 'expose his whole Soul' to examination—this is the place for genuine communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship doubles joy and divides grief
rubrics_metrics.description: A faithful friend improves happiness and lessens misery by sharing pleasures and should be regarded as a principal good in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical authorities (Tully, Bacon, Wisdom of Ben Sirach) are invoked: friendship is a 'treasure' and 'medicine of life'; one should cultivate friends prudently and value faithful companionship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of a good friend
rubrics_metrics.description: Key qualities of a good friend include constancy and faithfulness, virtue, knowledge, discretion, equality in age and fortune, pleasantness of temper (morum comitas), and evenness of behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware friends who are inconsistent in humour (difficilis, facilis...); test friends over time; value evenness so latent bad humours do not suddenly reveal themselves and make companionship unlivable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid betrayals that destroy friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain offences are fatal to friendship: disclosing secrets, upbraiding, pride, treachery, and grievous wounds against a friend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some breaches (sword-drawing, reviling) may permit reconciliation, betraying secrets is irreversible: 'he that bewrayeth Secrets, is without Hope.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Have many well-wishers but few counsellors
rubrics_metrics.description: It is prudent to have many who wish you well but to choose few trusted counsellors—'Be in Peace with many, nevertheless have but one Counsellor of a thousand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove friends before trusting them; a new friend is like new wine—time mellows value. Do not be hasty to credit anyone as a true friend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of thought and language in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity of thought pleases readers of all ranks; an ornate or 'Gothick' manner only pleases those with artificial taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdote: Molière testing plays by an old housekeeper's reception; the popular ballad ('Chevy Chase') pleases common people and was valued even by Ben Jonson. Simple, natural painting of nature reaches the broadest audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroic poem should embody a national moral precept
rubrics_metrics.description: A heroic (epic) poem should be founded on an important precept of morality adapted to the constitution or needs of the poet's country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homer and Virgil structured their epics to teach civic precepts appropriate to their societies (e.g., unity against common enemies). The poet should draw a clear moral or precept from the action, as in the concluding lines of popular heroic poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate persons/actions that honour the country
rubrics_metrics.description: An epic or heroic poem should celebrate persons and actions that do honour to the poet's country—raise national reputation by selecting relevant heroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism of poets who choose foreign or inappropriate subjects (Valerius Flaccus, Statius) suggests poets should select subjects that contribute to national honour and instruct citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select subject appropriate to the poet's nation
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet's subject ought to be suitable to his country (e.g., Roman poets praising Roman founders), not an exotic theme disconnected from national character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing local or nationally resonant subject matter helps the poem serve moral and civic instruction; foreign themes may expose the poet to derision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular song/ballad criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A song or ballad that is universally approved by common people demonstrates a certain perfection of simplicity and natural appeal—this quality is praiseworthy even when the style is plain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The success of 'old' songs among common listeners (and the admiration of poets like Ben Jonson and Sidney) is evidence that plain materials of nature can be elevated and more widely effective than ornate epigrams for broad audiences.
